$comment: Where Docxcelerate gets submitted, and what each destination asks for. `fields` are dot-paths into project.json - submit.mjs resolves them, so a target never carries its own copy. `limits` are character caps the renderer enforces; where a cap is unverified it is left out and called out in `notes` instead. `type`: pr = open a pull request, form = fill a web form, post = write a post, auto = happens without you.

targets.name: Libraries.io
targets.notes: Indexes from the npm registry within a day of a publish. Nothing to submit - but it reads description, homepage, keywords and license straight from package.json, which is why those were fixed first. Verify the page looks right after the next release.

targets.name: GitHub repository topics
targets.notes: Already set: 10 topics, homepage points at docxcelerate.com. GitHub topic search and every scraper that reads the repo API key off these. Re-check against topics in project.json when that list changes.

targets.name: awesome-nodejs
targets.notes: One line, in the form '- [name](repo) - Description.' Sentence case, ends with a period, no marketing adjectives - the maintainers reject copy that reads like a pitch. Read contributing.md before opening the PR; it is strict and the bar is real usage.

targets.name: awesome-typescript
targets.notes: Same one-line format as awesome-nodejs. Lower traffic, but it is a cheap PR once the line is written.

targets.name: OpenAlternative
targets.notes: Ranks open-source tools as alternatives to commercial ones, so the alternativeTo entries are the submission - not decoration. Requires a public repo with a detectable licence and real release history; it reads stars, commits and licence off the GitHub API.

targets.name: AlternativeTo
targets.notes: Needs an account with some standing before submissions get approved quickly. Each alternativeTo entry is added separately after the listing is live. Platform checkboxes come from platforms.

targets.name: StackShare
targets.notes: Slow-moving and low-traffic now, but it is a durable backlink and takes five minutes once the copy pack is rendered.

targets.name: SaaSHub
targets.notes: Aggregates into a lot of 'alternatives to X' SEO pages. Same alternativeTo framing as OpenAlternative.

targets.name: Product Hunt
targets.notes: Tagline is hard-capped at 60 characters. Needs at least three gallery images sized 1270x760 - assets.screenshots is empty, so this is blocked until those exist. Launch 12:01am PT; a developer tool with no screenshots gets buried.

targets.name: Hacker News (Show HN)
targets.notes: Title form: 'Show HN: Docxcelerate - <what it does>', 80 characters including the 18-character prefix. Link to docxcelerate.com, then post the blurb as the first comment with what is genuinely unfinished. Weekday morning US Eastern. One shot - a flagged repost does not get a second.

targets.name: Lobste.rs
targets.notes: Invite-only to post. Tags: javascript, programming. Audience is hostile to anything that reads as marketing; the docs page is a better link than the landing page here.

targets.name: Reddit (r/javascript, r/node, r/typescript)
targets.notes: r/javascript allows self-promotion on Showoff Saturday only - check each subreddit's rules, they differ and they enforce. Space the three posts over days, not hours. Lead with the problem and the code sample, link second.

targets.name: dev.to launch article
targets.notes: Long-form is what this is for: the JSX-component-tree argument, with the tenancy-renewal example built end to end. Canonical-URL it to a post on docxcelerate.com so the site keeps the SEO. Tags: javascript, typescript, node, opensource.

targets.name: JavaScript Weekly / Node Weekly
targets.notes: Curated by a human, and a single mention moves more real developers than most of the directories above. Submit once the README, licence and a screenshot are all in place - one shot per project, effectively.

targets.name: Console.dev
targets.notes: Newsletter for developer tools. Editorially selected, no cost, low effort to submit.

targets.name: npm keyword surfaces
targets.notes: npm's own keyword pages, and every 'best docx library' listicle that scrapes them, rank on keywords in package.json. Now 16 terms wide. No action beyond publishing.
